aiia.prompt.text:
Here is the official context of the MyKTAMap application (attached .md file or text pasted below).

You will help me use it by following these STRICT rules:

⛔ Answer ONLY from the content of the provided context.
⛔ If a feature is not described in it, say so clearly — NEVER make things up.
⛔ Do not extrapolate from other apps (Google Maps, QGIS, etc.).
⛔ You have access neither to the source code, nor the website, nor my application.
✅ Cite the section of the context where you find the info (e.g. "According to the Route recipe…").
✅ Use the exact icons and labels mentioned in the doc, with concrete steps.
✅ Always answer in MY language.
✅ If a "🔧 Installation state" block is present at the end of the context, use it for troubleshooting.

If you have understood, simply reply "OK, ready" and wait for my first question.

home.netdoc.docOutro: (Opens in a new tab — it is a static file served by the same Nginx as the app.)
home.netdoc.lead: MyKTAMap is a 100% client-side PWA. Everything you create (annotations, sessions, saved maps, KMZ calibrations, preferences) stays in your browser. The Nginx server only serves static files. No application backend, no server database, no analytics, no tracking cookie.
home.netdoc.quote: « If you find anything that contradicts this page, contact me (Instagram @karma_kta or contact@myktamap.fr) — I will fix it immediately. »
home.netdoc.scope1: This security and no-telemetry guarantee applies ONLY to the official domain myktamap.fr.
home.netdoc.scope2: MyKTAMap's source code is public (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and can be copied, forked or mirrored by anyone. Any third-party install — whatever name or domain it uses, even one claiming to be « MyKTAMap » — may contain modifications we are not responsible for: added tracking, data exfiltration, injected malicious code. We have no way to verify what goes on there.
home.netdoc.scope3: How to make sure you are on the real site? Check the URL in your browser's address bar. If it does not start with https://myktamap.fr, nothing written on this page concerns you — it is a copy we have no control over.
home.netdoc.title: 📖 What does the app do on the network?
home.netdoc.verify1: Internal log: the « 📋 View the network log » button in the same section — logs in real time every request the app emits.
home.netdoc.verify2: Browser DevTools (F12): « Network » tab → you see every request, regardless of what the app claims. Filter by method to confirm there is no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
home.netdoc.verify3: A single outside site: the OpenStreetMap background of the OSM View (tile.openstreetmap.org). Untick the « 🗺️ OSM View » box in the same section (or switch to incognito mode): the app then only contacts its own server — the log and F12 show it.
home.netdoc.verify4: Content Security Policy: F12 → Network → first request (HTML) → Headers tab → look for Content-Security-Policy. The Nginx server tells the browser to block any non-whitelisted connection: only the site itself and the OpenStreetMap background are allowed.

lost.tips.attendre.1: Settle in an identifiable spot (numbered shaft, named chamber, visible marking).
lost.tips.attendre.2: Stay where you are if nobody knows you're there — moving makes things worse.
lost.tips.attendre.3: Mark your location (paint, tape, a bright bag) so you can be found.
lost.tips.calme.1: Stop. Breathe in. Sit down for a few seconds.
lost.tips.calme.2: Panic makes you lose your bearings and wastes light + energy.
lost.tips.calme.3: Eat/drink a little if you have something. Catch your breath.
lost.tips.comm.1: If you get a signal (often near shafts / under certain manholes) → tell someone on the surface BEFORE your battery dies.
lost.tips.comm.2: The 📋 Copy report button below prepares a ready-made message with your last position + elapsed time.
lost.tips.lumiere.1: Switch your lamp to economy mode. Dead lamp = serious situation.
lost.tips.lumiere.2: Keep a backup lamp if you have one (headlamp + pen light is ideal).
lost.tips.lumiere.3: Hydrate a little but ration it — stress dehydrates you fast.
lost.tips.nepas.1: Don't follow the water — fissures often lead to dangerous narrow passages.
lost.tips.nepas.2: Don't attempt an unknown passage just because it seems to go up / head "toward the outside".
lost.tips.nepas.3: Don't trust the phone tracker — it drifts, especially under stress (erratic movements).
lost.tips.orient.1: Retrace your steps rather than trying to reach your destination — statistically more reliable.
lost.tips.orient.2: Look for the main axes (main galleries, straight galleries, railway tracks). They almost always lead to a known landmark.
lost.tips.orient.3: Use a physical compass — not the phone's, distorted by the ground and metal framework. Re-orient yourself at every junction.
lost.tips.orient.4: Listen to the sounds: traffic, subway, train, running water = useful directional clue.

lost.vitesse.hint: 💡 Choose based on the presumed state of the lost person. The search radius = speed × elapsed time. Same values as the route mode for consistency.

oom.kill.howTitle: 💡 How to avoid it happening again
oom.kill.intro: Last time, the app shut down abruptly and couldn't save its session normally.
oom.kill.tip.closeApps: Close other background apps before using MyKTAMap. On iPhone: double-tap Home or swipe up + dismiss the cards. On Android: multitask button + swipe away.
oom.kill.tip.export: Export your session regularly (📤 Export) so you lose nothing in case of an abrupt shutdown.
oom.kill.tip.optimize: If the problem persists on a specific map, its main image may be too large — it then needs re-optimizing (PNG compression or smaller dimensions).
oom.kill.tip.perf: Lower the performance mode in the loader (🚀 icon or via ⚙️ Settings). "Performance" loads smaller tiles and uses less RAM than "Quality".
oom.kill.tip.tabs: Avoid opening multiple browser tabs at once if you use the app via Safari/Chrome — each tab also uses memory.
oom.kill.tip.update: Keep your smartphone up to date: iOS and Android regularly improve their memory management for PWAs.
oom.kill.whyBody: On smartphones (iOS and Android), the operating system silently kills tabs and installed apps that use too much RAM. That's very often what happened here, especially if you're using a high-resolution map or many other apps were running at the same time.
oom.v2.explain: It's very likely a browser memory overload — V2 conversion decodes the source image at full resolution then generates N tiles, which can exceed the memory cap of mobile browsers (~500 MB on iOS Safari, variable on Android).
oom.v2.intro: Last time, you were running the V2 conversion of map {nom} (image {taille}) and the app shut down abruptly before it finished.
oom.v2.sol.closeApps: Close other apps in the background to free up RAM before retrying.
oom.v2.sol.pc: Do the conversion on a PC (Windows / macOS / Linux). No memory cap in practice. Once the V2 ZIP is generated, import it on your phone — the import is lightweight (no full-resolution decoding).
oom.v2.sol.resize: Shrink the source image to 6000-8000 px max before retrying (GIMP / Photoshop / Squoosh).

tutorial.card.bienvenue.texte:
MyKTAMap is a map for the underground: quarries, galleries, underground sites. It works on the image of a map, without GPS or network.

🔒 Your maps, notes and photos stay on your phone: nothing is sent anywhere.

This tutorial covers the essentials. You can replay it at any time from 📖 Documentation → 🎓.
tutorial.card.bienvenue.hint: Move on with ◂ ▸; on a computer, with the ← → arrows or Enter.
tutorial.card.avant-de-descendre.texte:
• 📱 Install the app on your home screen (share menu ↑ or ⋮ → “Add to Home Screen”). On iPhone, do it before loading your maps.
  • 📡 Open it once with a network connection and load your map: it is kept in the app. The green dot next to the version number, at the bottom of the home screen, confirms everything is ready.
  • 🕳️ After that, everything works offline, underground as on the surface.

When a new version exists and you have a connection, the app offers to update.
tutorial.card.charger.texte:
On the home screen:

  • 📚 My maps — every map you have already opened; a tap reopens it.
  • 📦 Add a map — drop your map's ZIP file on the area, then ▶️ Load this map.
  • ▶️ Resume — reopens the last map you used.

Want to create your own map? 🏗️ Generate a map: it is all explained in 📖 Documentation → “Going further”.
tutorial.card.urgence.texte:
• 🚨 Emergency exit (top of the screen) — you want to get out fast: the app finds the nearest exit and draws the way.
  • 🔆 XL display (🧭 Tracker menu) — you know where you are: the map around you and your compass in very large print, plus your GPS coordinates to read out to rescuers if the map is georeferenced.
  • ⛑️ I'm lost (🧭 Tracker menu) — you no longer know where you are: the app estimates the area where you may be.

To coordinate search teams, Rescue mode is described in the Documentation.
tutorial.card.urgence.hint: The app never replaces rescue services: always tell someone on the surface before going down.
tutorial.card.interface.titre: Finding your way around the app
tutorial.card.interface.texte:
• At the top: the map name, your counters (📍 🛣️ ⬛ 🏛️ 📸 → your session details), 📖 Story Mode (the map's notes and documents) and 🌍 OSM View if the map is placed on the world map.
  • On the sides: two toolbars; only one group opens at a time.
  • At the bottom: what is running (measurement, route, tracking).

📚 → Legend explains the icons; ≡ Filters chooses what is shown. On a multi-storey map, the yellow pill under the zoom shows the level.
tutorial.card.chercher.texte:
🔍 Search (or Ctrl+K) finds a point, path, zone or structure by its name; a tap centres the map on it.

⭐ In a point's bubble, ☆ Favorite keeps it in ⭐ Favorites so you can come back to it in one move.
tutorial.card.suivre.texte:
Without GPS, the tracker counts your steps and follows your direction with the phone's sensors.

  • 🧭 Tracker → Start / stop tracking: your icon moves with you and draws your path.
  • Realign often: 📍 I am here on a point you recognise, or Realignment mode then a tap where you are.
  • Show the compass gives you North.
tutorial.card.suivre.hint: The position drifts with every step: realigning about every 50 m keeps it accurate.
tutorial.card.itineraire.texte:
In a point's bubble, 🧭 Go there computes the way from your position, along the map's galleries. For several stops: 🧭 Tracker → Compute a route.

🪧 As you walk, a banner guides you: “In 40 m, turn left”. ⛔ Inaccessible zones are avoided.
tutorial.card.annoter.texte:
• ✏️ Editing — add your points (with 📸 photos).
  • 🛣️ Paths — draw the galleries: routes go through them.
  • ⬛ Zones — water, backfill, collapse… ⛔ Inaccessible blocks routes.
  • 🏛️ Structures — pillars, walls, working faces.
  • 📐 Measure — a distance or an area.

A mistake? ⏪ Undo (Ctrl+Z).
tutorial.card.donnees.texte:
• 💾 Everything is saved automatically, map by map, with backups you can restore (top counters → 📦 Recent backups).
  • 📔 My logbook keeps the history of your outings: date, duration, path walked.
  • ⬆️ Save exports your session, the map as an image or PDF, or a file for Google Earth and GPS apps.

Everything is on your device: export what you want to keep elsewhere.

__comment_aide: ❓ Aide integree — migree du HTML en dur (js/interfaceDocs.js) vers les dicos, lot 2. 1 intro + 32 titres + 32 corps HTML. Le HTML est VOULU dans la valeur : ce sont des sections de doc mises en forme, pas des libellés.
aide.intro: One short page per feature, sorted like the guide; the search looks through their titles and content, and the ❓ button of a window opens its page directly. For the details: 📖 Documentation.
aide.sec.histoire.titre: 📖 Story Mode — the map's note and documents
aide.sec.histoire.html:
The 📖 button on the right of the top bar, next to 🚨. A window with two tabs, specific to each map:

  • 📝 Free note — saved as you type. ✏️ Edit opens the text with a formatting bar (bold, headings, lists, links…), 👁 Preview returns to the rendered view.
  • 📚 Story — up to 10 PDF documents per map. 📥 Import a PDF adds one, 🗑️ Remove deletes the one displayed. Documents shipped with the map (📕) come first; once removed, they come back the next time the map is opened. On iPhone, ↗️ Open in a tab shows the document full screen.

Warning above 25 MB of documents, refusal above 100 MB. The note and documents go with the session export (except the anonymised export) and can also be read in 📔 My logbook › Stories, without loading the map. Details: 📖 Documentation › 📖 Story Mode.
aide.sec.sortie-urgence.html:
To get out right now. The 🚨 button on the right of the top bar, next to 📖 — or say « sortie » to the 🎤 voice command (French only: the 🎤 button only appears when the app is in French).

  1. The app looks for points marked as an open exit (Open quarry access, Open rung shaft, Open service stairs) or as an entrance, including “Plan entry point”. An access marked closed is never suggested.
  2. It computes the real path through the galleries, including from one level to another.
  3. The window shows the nearest one (distance, level), the 🧭 Plot the route button and the ▾ Show the N other exits fold-out.

The computation starts from your position as soon as tracking is on or you have located yourself once since opening the map; the window tells you which. If you have never located yourself, the app asks Where are you?: tap your position on the map (that tap also realigns tracking).

An exit marked Straight-line distance — route not verified has no computed path: it may be unreachable. Once the route is drawn, the guidance banner stays on screen; if you stray, its button becomes Nearest exit from here. A vibration confirms the result, even when vibration is turned off. Everything is computed without network.

Position and heading in very large type → 🔆 XL display page. You no longer know where you are → ⛑️ I'm lost page. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🆘 In an emergency underground.
aide.sec.aide-doc-legende.html:
The 📚 Help / Documentation / Legend group in the left sidebar opens three windows:

❓Help — these short pages, one per feature.📖Documentation — the full guide, also on the home screen (📖 button). In its title row, 🎓 replays the tutorial and 🤖 opens AI Help.🗺️Legend — every icon, path and zone → 🏷️ Legend page.

🔎 Search. The field at the top of 📖 Documentation searches the whole text: results are highlighted, Enter or ↓ moves to the next one, and the table of contents fades where nothing matches. Accents do not matter.

🤖 AI Help: downloads a file describing the app, to attach to the conversational AI of your choice before asking your questions. It contains none of your data.

🚨 Public alerts: a safety alert broadcast by the author shows up at launch (red = critical, orange = important, blue = announcement). The 🚨 button on the home screen, left of 📖, shows them again or confirms there is none.

Details: 📖 Documentation › 📚 Help and documentation.
aide.sec.parametres.html:
Two settings screens, depending on what they affect:

🏠⚙️ Configuration (top of the home screen) — the whole app: language, display, notifications, light theme, 🧩 Optional features, logbook, incognito mode, 🔐 Local access code, 🆘 Troubleshooting (forced update, reset).🗺️⚙️ Settings (sidebar, map open) — this map: scale and 🎯 calibration, North, GPS georeferencing, tracker start, step detection, 🚀 ULTRA mode, presentation mode. Each group states its scope: 📍 this map or 🌍 all maps.

No Apply button: everything is saved as soon as you change it, and an out-of-range value turns red while the old one is kept. ↺ Default values, at the bottom of ⚙️ Settings, only puts this map back to its original values; to reset the whole app → 🆘 Troubleshooting card.

Details: 📖 Documentation › ⚙️ My maps and settings.
aide.sec.recherche.html:
The 🔍 button in the sidebar, or Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac), opens the search; Ctrl+K again closes it. Results appear as you type, sorted by category: 📍 Points · 🛣️ Paths · ⬛ Zones · 🏛️ Structures.

  • What is searched: a point's name, identifier, tags, description and state; the name, type and level of a path, zone or structure — your additions as well as the map's layers. Accents and capitals are ignored.
  • Pick one: ↑ / ↓ then Enter, or tap a result; the map centres on it and its form opens.
  • Filters under the field: category, and for points, layers and tags. ✕ Clear filters removes them.
  • GPS coordinates (georeferenced map): paste 48.856600, 2.352200 → 🎯 Go to point if a point is very close, otherwise ➕ Create a point here.
  • Search across all plans: your query across your whole library, without opening the maps — also from the 🔎 bar on the home screen. A click opens the right map, centred on the point.

Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔍 Unified search.
aide.sec.charger-import.html:
📥Import a file (session or GPX) — the ⬇️ Load / Import button opens the file picker directly. A session (.json, or .zip with photos) replaces yours, after an automatic backup; a GPX adds its points and paths to a georeferenced map (Ctrl+Z to undo).📊Plan data editor — in ⬆️ Export, 💾 Session section: your data as a table; it also holds 🔗 Merge data layers and 🔁 Realign data onto another scan.

Adding a map: on the home screen, 📦 Add a map, drop the ZIP then ▶️ Load this map. With “💾 Store the map in the app on first load” (⚙️ Configuration, on by default), it reopens in one tap, even offline; otherwise its ZIP is asked for each time you open it.

Same name as a map in your list, whatever the author and version: the app asks 🔄 Update (session, notes and links kept), ➕ Keep both or Cancel, the default choice.

📦 Import several maps (🧰 Tools) adds a batch of ZIPs without opening them. In the ℹ️ sheet of a stored map, 💾 Download the ZIP gives you its archive back. Details: 📖 Documentation › 📦 Load a map.
aide.sec.import-sig.html:
Turns a GIS export into a MyKTAMap map. Drop your file (.geojson, .json, .kml, .kmz) on 📦 Add a map on the home screen, or in the Generator: 🗺️ Convert from GIS opens.

  • No image needed: a blank background is aligned on the file's coordinates.
  • Mapping: pick the column that holds the type, then what each value stands for. Each value can target any family: a polygon can become a zone, a path, a pillar or a working face.
  • Level column: one floor per value, with One colour per level and 🏷️ to rename them.
  • You give the width, the height is computed.

Coordinates in WGS84 or Lambert 93 (converted, check the resulting position); any other projection is refused. A warning above 20,000 objects, refusal above 60,000. Shapefile and GeoPackage: re-export as GeoJSON. A misclassified object can then be fixed in 🔍 Filters → 📊 Data layers → 🔄 Edit. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🗺️ Convert a GIS file (QGIS…).
aide.sec.creer-modifier-plan.html:
🛠️ For map creators.

The 🏗️ button in the sidebar opens the Generator (📦 Create / Edit a map), which produces a map's ZIP archive.

🧙🧙 Wizard — step by step, ⏭ Skip for the optional steps, then a ✅ Summary before generation that flags what is missing. 🗒️ Show all shows the whole form at once.⚙️🚀 Simple or ⚙️ Advanced — the essentials (image, name, version), or every option: layers, icons, georeferencing, legend.📂📂 Load a file — a map's ZIP to edit it, or a KMZ, a GPX, a GIS export (GeoJSON, KML) or a georeferenced GeoTIFF whose georeferencing and scale are picked up.🧱🧱 Convert to V2 tiles — splits a large image to lighten memory use; do it on a computer.🔄🔄 Update the map — from an open map (⬆️ Export, or ≡ Filters at the top of the layers): your corrected layers and drawings go into the pre-filled Generator, then the map is replaced in the app or published as a new version.

📦 Generate ZIP downloads the archive. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🏗️ Create or edit a map.
aide.sec.bibliotheque-plans.html:
⭐Pin — the star moves the map to the top.ℹ️Map sheet — details, Rename display, Map tags, 💾 Download the ZIP, 🗑️ Remove from list.🔎🔎 Filter by name… — plus tag filter chips.📁Folders — All | Folders; file a map by dragging it or with Select several maps → Move to….🌐🌐 Show server maps — hides or shows the server's maps.

⚠️ Removing a map erases its session, georeferencing, photos and backups (not the ZIP on your disk). Details: 📖 Documentation › 📚 Your map list.
aide.sec.profil.html:
The home screen's profile banner opens 👤 Profile: nickname, photo, wallpaper, rank and 🏆 Achievements.

📊Your statistics — counters and the 📊 My maps table; 🎨 Home banner stats picks what the banner shows.🖼️🖼️ Home wallpaper — your image; its metadata (including location) is removed.📤📤 Export my profile — a file to change device (maps, preferences, sessions, logbook…).📥📥 Import a profile — 🔄 Merge adds without overwriting (recommended), ♻️ Replace first empties the ticked sections.

The access code, the PIN and the wallpaper image are never exported. Details: 📖 Documentation › 👤 Profile.
aide.sec.favoris.html:
Mark the points you want to find again in one tap: entrance, meeting point, landmark room.

☆☆ Favorite — in a point's bubble, adds the point to your favorites or removes it (the button turns into ⭐ Favorite).⭐⭐ Favorites — group in the left sidebar: the list of favorites for the open map. A tap centres the map on the point, circles it and opens its bubble.📤Sharing — 📊 Session details → ⭐ Favorites: Export (current map), Export (all maps), Import a JSON (adds without creating duplicates).

Favorites are kept per map on your device and also travel with the profile export. A favorite keeps a copy of the point: it stays in the list even if the point is moved or deleted.
aide.sec.historique-undo.html:
⏪Undo — Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on Mac)⏩Redo — Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z

Both buttons are in the ⏪ History group, at the bottom of the sidebar; they are greyed out when there is nothing to do. The last 50 actions are kept, and a message says what was undone or redone.

Can be undone: adding, editing, moving and deleting points; each point placed on a path, zone or structure, closing them and deleting them; conversions.

Cannot be undone: deleting a photo, importing a session, position tracking, measurement. The history is forgotten when you reload the page or change map. Details: 📖 Documentation › ⏪ Undo / Redo.
aide.sec.batterie.html:
🧩 Optional feature, off by default: turn it on in ⚙️ Configuration › 🧩 Optional features. Takes effect the next time the app starts.

The remaining charge is shown at the top of the screen (⚡ charging, 🪫 discharging, colour by level) and in the 🔆 XL display.

🔋20% — a message suggests 🚀 ULTRA mode to save power.🪫10% — a message suggests ULTRA and stopping the tracker, which uses a lot of sensors.🚨5% — red 🪫 Critical battery window: save your session, note your position, consider heading back up.

Each alert shows only once per discharge. Only Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet give the battery level to web pages: on Safari and Firefox, the indicator stays hidden. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🔋 Battery level.
aide.sec.stats-session.html:
Tapping the counters at the top opens 📊 Session details, the map's dashboard.

  • At the top, ✅ Saved … ago (in red if saving fails).
  • The totals: points, paths, zones, structures, total length of paths, area of zones, photos, time since the map was opened; the per-level breakdown on a multi-level map. 📋 Copy puts this summary on the clipboard, 📤 Export as TXT downloads it.
  • The list of what you added, other measurements, the 📔 Trip in progress and your ⭐ Favorites (→ the 📔 My logbook and ⭐ Favorites sheets).
  • 📦 Recent backups of this map: ↻ Restore, 📆 Snapshot now, 🗑️ Clear all — every deletion asks for confirmation.
  • 🗑️ Clear the session: the same clearing as the “Previous session restored” window, at any time (a copy stays in 📦 Backups).
  • 📊 View the map's global statistics: your session plus the map's data layers, with report, CSV and PDF.

Details: 📖 Documentation › 📊 Session statistics.
aide.sec.inspecteur-memoire.html:
Shows what the app takes up on your device: the space used and the browser's quota, the detail of what is stored (settings, sessions, photos, backups, app files) and the latest abrupt shutdowns detected.

📊Opening it — from the home screen, ⚙️ Configuration › 🛠️ System & maintenance › 📊 View memory state.🧹🧹 Orphan data — what is left of maps removed from your list; Clean all deletes it, after confirmation. The logbook and stories are always kept.📋📋 Copy the report — a text summary to attach when you report a problem.

Everything is read on your device, nothing is sent. Details: 📖 Documentation › ⚙️ My maps and settings › ⚙️ Configuration (home screen).
aide.sec.legende.html:
📚 Help / Documentation / Legend → Legend lists icons, paths, zones and structures. ✏️ Edit customizes each type:

✏️Rename — your label shows everywhere.🎨Colour — applied at once to the map, exports and OSM View; ↺ restores the original.👁️Hide — removes the entry from the legend only; for the map, use ≡ Filters.➕➕ Add an entry — your own type, drawable right away (also: New type… in the drawing menus).🗑️Delete one of your types — the app tells you how many objects still use it.

Saved per map, it travels with your exports. A map's creator can set its legend for everyone (Generator 🏗️ › 🏷️ Map legend).

Details: 📖 Documentation › 🗺️ Using the map › 🗺️ Legend.
aide.sec.menu-tracker.html:
The 🧭 Tracker button (or the 🧭 light in the bottom bar) opens a full-screen window of large tiles. At the top: Tracking on or Tracking off, the distance walked and the number of steps.

▶️Tracking — start / stop tracking, 📍 Realignment mode, 🎯 My position, 🔓 Suspend trace lock (when smart navigation is turned on).🧰Tools — 🧭 Compass, 🗺️ Compute a route, 🪧 Itinerary guidance, 🗺️ Oriented map. 🎬 Replay and 🔥 Heatmap are added here when you turn them on.🚨Emergency (red background) — ⛑️ I'm lost, 🔆 XL display, 🚑 Rescue mode.

Tapping a tile closes the window and runs the action; ✕, a tap outside or Esc close it without doing anything. Each tile has its own card (🧭 Tracker, 🗺️ Routes and 🪧 guidance, ⛑️ I'm lost, 🔆 XL display…). Details: 📖 Documentation › 📍 Position tracker.
aide.sec.replay-tracker.html:
🧩 Optional feature, off by default: turn it on in ⚙️ Configuration › 🧩 Optional features.

The 🎬 tile of the 🧭 Tracker menu replays your tracking session: a yellow marker retraces your path and the trail grows as it goes.

▶️Playback — time slider, play / pause, speed from 0.5× to 10×. ⛶ shrinks the window to the bottom of the screen so you can see the map.⌨️Keyboard — Space: play / pause · ← →: one second back / forward · Esc: close.📤📤 Export CSV — the timestamped positions (and the level on a multi-level map), readable in a spreadsheet.

A recalibration shows as a jump, with no line drawn. The replay starts from scratch when the app reloads or the map changes. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🎬 Tracker replay.
aide.sec.enregistrer.html:
Every export starts from the ⬆️ Export group of the side bar: it opens a tile launcher in three parts.

  • 🖼️ Image — Image (PNG / JPEG): ⚡ Quick mode (what is visible, as PNG) or 🎨 Advanced mode (layers, legend, format, resolution); 🖨️ Printable PDF: A0 to A4, portrait or landscape, legend in a corner.
  • 💾 Session — Full export: your whole session in one re-importable file (.json, or .zip with the photos), tracker trail included; 🛡️ Anonymise for public sharing replaces names with codes and removes the trail. Advanced export: you choose what to export, by category and by type.
  • 🌍 External export — KMZ (Google Earth, OsmAnd…) or GPX, for a georeferenced map.

Turning your session into a data layer (🔄 Conversion) or merging several layers (🔗 Merge) is done in the 📊 Data editor.

If the map's levels have a depth, the KMZ places the survey below the surface; the GPX writes it in the description. Before sharing, check that nothing reveals an access or a private place. Details: 📖 Documentation › ⬆️ Save and share.
aide.sec.tracker.html:
The tracker estimates your position without GPS, using the phone's motion sensors (steps and direction).

  1. ▶️ Start: the warning window offers to keep the screen on; confirm with Got it — Start and allow access to the sensors.
  2. Your icon follows your walk and a trail records your path. ⏹️ stops tracking.
  3. Realign yourself about every 50 m: the 📍 Realignment mode tile, then tap where you are, or 📍 I am here in a point's popup.

🧭 Compass shows a compass rose; 🎯 My position re-centres the map on you.

Settings: ⚙️ Settings › 📍 Navigation & tracker. The start position is specific to each map; step detection (step length, threshold, delay) applies to all your maps. Everything depends on the map's scale: check it first. Lost → ⛑️ I'm lost card; vital info in big print → 🔆 XL display; a way to go → 🗺️ Routes and 🪧 guidance. Details: 📖 Documentation › 📍 Position tracker.
aide.sec.mode-secours.html:
👥 For the leaders who organize the search for a person missing underground, and the teams who go down to look for them. If you are the one who is lost → ⛑️ I'm lost card.

To open it: 🧭 Tracker menu → at the bottom, on a red background, 🚑 Rescue mode — Search plans (teams + zones). Prerequisite: the same map on every phone, available offline.

  1. Prepare — ➕ New scenario, then the teams, their route, their zone and the computed itinerary.
  2. Hand over — 📤 Export .mkmsec.json to each team, which opens it with 📥 Import a plan; PDF sheets and KMZ as a complement.
  3. Follow — 🚀 Launch the rescue plan, then everyone chooses their role: 👤 Surface operator, 🚨 Field team or 🚑 Free rescuer.
  4. Close — the operator gathers the teams' reports (📥 Import team report) and produces the final 📤 Report.

Prepare a scenario in advance on your usual maps: on the day, the app has to be ready in 30 seconds. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🚑 Rescue mode — coordinating a search.
aide.sec.mesure.titre: 📐 Measure a distance or an area
aide.sec.vue-osm.titre: 🌍 OSM View — your maps on the world map
aide.sec.vue-osm.html:
Lays your georeferenced maps on OpenStreetMap, with their objects and your additions. Access: the 🌍 OSM View widget on the home screen, or the 🌍 button on a map (opened at least once).

📏Measure — distance and area.🎯Surface coordinates — a click, then Copy: to pass on to a team at the surface.🗂️Several maps — ≡ button: order, opacity, content per map.🗺️Legend — the map's legend, read-only (edit it from the map).💾💾 Save Offline — the background map of the visible area.

Accuracy depends on the map's georeferencing.

🔒 The only screen that goes online (OpenStreetMap background, none of your data). Turn it off in ⚙️ Configuration › 🔒 Privacy & Audit. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🌍 OSM View.
aide.sec.mesure.html:
In the 📐 Measurement group:

📐Distance — tap points: the total appears at the bottom left, with the length of each segment and the angles.♦️Surface — tap at least 3 points: the area appears in m², then in hectares beyond 10,000 m².❌Erase — ↩️ Last point (on the lit measurement), the whole distance, the whole surface, or both.

The two measurements coexist: your next tap goes to the one that is lit. They are kept with your session and their accuracy depends on the map's scale (⚙️ Settings). The total length of the galleries → 🛣️ Paths card (📏 Total distance); a way to go → 🗺️ Routes and 🪧 guidance. Details: 📖 Documentation › 📐 Distance and ♦️ area measurement.
aide.sec.edition-points.html:
1. Press ✏️ (it lights up): every tap on the map places a point.
  2. Fill in the Name (required), the Type (it sets the icon) and a Description if you like.
  3. Confirm with ✅ Add. Press ✏️ again to leave the mode.

📸 Photos: up to 5 per point, via 📷 Take photo or 🖼️ From gallery. They stay on your device, compressed and stripped of their GPS position. Deleting a point does not delete its photos: 🧰 Tools › 📸 My photos (home screen) finds them, to attach them to a point or recreate the point.

A point's popup (tap the marker): 📍 I am here recalibrates tracking on this point, 🧭 Go there, ➕ Route, ☆ Favorite, 🔊 reads the note. On your points: ✏️ Edit, 📌 Reposition (your next tap moves the point, everything else is kept) and 🗑️ Delete this point.

A photo's date taken is kept beside it (never in the file): "Taken on …" in full screen. A ⚠️ Danger point carries a 📅 date observed (today by default, editable) shown in its popup, with this reminder: MyKTAMap does not certify the condition of a site, a recorded hazard may have changed since.

Everything can be undone with ⏪ (Ctrl+Z). Deleting → 🧹 Erase, convert, correct card. Details: 📖 Documentation › ✏️ Add points.
aide.sec.structures.html:
In the 🏛️ Structures group, the load-bearing elements and the progress of the workings:

🟡1st-mass pillar — yellow surface🟠2nd-mass pillar — orange surface🔵Wall — blue surface🟨1st-mass quarry face — yellow line🟧2nd-mass quarry face — orange line

Press a type, tap the points, then press the lit type again (or ✅ Close the current structure): a pillar or a wall (3 points minimum) closes up, a quarry face (2 points minimum) stays a line.

Structures have no effect on the route. On a multi-storey map, the 2nd mass is placed one level below the active level. A quarry face that is really a gallery, erasing or deleting → 🧹 Erase, convert, correct card. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🏛️ Structures (pillars, walls, quarry faces).
aide.sec.traces.html:
In the 🛣️ Paths group: 🟩 Main road, 🟪 Secondary road, 🟨 Path. Press a type, tap the map point by point, then press the type again (or ✅ Confirm the current path) to finish.

Paths are the network the route is calculated on: a gallery that is not drawn does not exist for it.

📏 Total distance adds up the length of every path on the map — yours and those of the data layers, even hidden ones, custom types included — with one box per type. The counted sections are highlighted in magenta; ❌ Clear highlight removes it.

🪜 Inter-level junction (multi-storey maps) → 🏗️ Multi-level card. Erasing, deleting or converting a path → 🧹 Erase, convert, correct card. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🛣️ Draw paths.
aide.sec.zones.html:
In the ⬛ Zones group, closed surfaces to annotate the map:

⬛Backfill — dark grey🟥Collapse — red🟦Water — blue⛔Inaccessible — dark red / black hatching: the route does not cross it

Press a type, place at least 3 points, then close the zone: tap the first point again (a circle surrounds it from the 3rd on) or press ✅ Close the current zone.

How routes deal with ⛔ zones → 🗺️ Routes and 🪧 guidance card. Erasing, deleting or converting a zone → 🧹 Erase, convert, correct card. Details: 📖 Documentation › ⬛ Draw zones.
aide.sec.optimiser-plan.html:
🛠️ For map creators.

A light map loads faster and crashes far less on mobile. From the most to the least effective:

🖼️Main image — 8,000 px per side at most, as JPEG quality 80 to 90% (often 5 to 10 times lighter than a PNG).🧱Large map — 🧱 Convert to V2 tiles in the Generator, on a computer.🗂️Image layers — ideally just one: merge legend and landmarks into the main image.🛣️Large network — galleries drawn in the image and the paths layer hidden: the itinerary still uses it.📍Many points — spread over several data layers that anyone can hide.

On a weak device: ⚙️ Settings › 🚀 Performance › 🚀 ULTRA mode (enables everything), for the open map. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🚀 Optimize your map.
aide.sec.code-acces.html:
🔐 Off by default: turn it on from the home screen, ⚙️ Configuration › 🔒 Privacy & security › 🔐 Local access code › 🔐 Enable access code.

Locks the app at every startup with a 4 to 6 digit code, or Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint / Windows Hello if your device supports it. Choose your code, confirm it, accept biometrics if offered, and write your code down somewhere safe.

✏️✏️ Change code or 🔓 Disable — same section, after confirming with biometrics or the current code.⏳5 wrong codes in a row — temporary lock: 10 min, then 1 h, 6 h and 24 h with each new series. The keypad comes back by itself when the delay is over; a correct code resets everything.

This is a usage barrier, not encryption: your photos and sessions remain readable in the browser by someone who knows how. The code stays on the device and cannot be recovered if you forget it. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🔐 Local access code (PIN / Face ID).
aide.sec.astuces.html:
• Only one group open at a time in the sidebars; touching outside closes it. The ≡ button at the top of a bar folds it away without stopping the current mode.
  • Only one mode on at a time (measurement, adding points, path, zone, realignment): turning one on stops the previous one. While a mode is on, its group stays open and its icon shows the current mode.
  • Opening a window (Settings, Filters, Documentation…) cancels the current mode. The tracker keeps running, and the form of a point you have just placed does not cancel editing.
  • Tapping an icon opens the point's form; double-tapping it zooms in on it.
  • Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) opens the search. On a computer, the ? key shows all keyboard shortcuts.

Details: 📖 Documentation › 🗺️ Using the map › 🧭 Interface overview.
aide.sec.depannage.html:
The common cases, from the simplest to the most drastic:

💥The app stops abruptly — memory is full: close other apps and turn on 🚀 ULTRA mode (⚙️ Settings › 🚀 Performance).⚠️⚠️ Plan not found — 🔄 Retry, 📁 Re-select the ZIP or 🗑️ Remove from list.📥The app isn't ready offline — the dot next to the version number, at the bottom of the home screen, is red: tap it with a connection to save everything. Green: everything is ready.🔌The 🔌 badge says "Invalid configuration" or "Licence required" — the installation you use declares a misconfigured database (never the case on myktamap.fr, which has none). Nothing is enabled and no data is sent: let the person who runs this installation know.🔄The app does not update — ⚙️ Configuration › 🆘 Troubleshooting › 🔄 Force the update (a connection is needed).🆘The app stays stuck — turn off your VPN or change network, then ⚙️ Configuration › 🆘 Troubleshooting › 🆘 Open the Kill SW tool. If it does not open at all: the rescue page https://myktamap.fr/killsw.html in a private tab of the browser.🧨💥 Reset everything (⚙️ Configuration › 🆘 Troubleshooting) — puts the app back as on a first launch and deletes everything, with no way back. First write down the community access code it shows.

Forced update, Kill SW and the rescue page delete no data; as a precaution, 📤 Export my profile first. Problem not solved: contact@myktamap.fr. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🆘 Troubleshooting.
aide.sec.liaisons-inter-plan.html:
A portal links a point on one map to a point on another map.

  • Create: a point's form → 🌀 Link to another plan → target map → arrival point.
  • Go through: 🌀 row of the form → ➜; the other map opens and your tracker realigns there. ↩️ Back: <map> takes you back for 15 s.
  • 🌀 My links (home screen): all your links, as a List or a Graph.
  • Route to another map: Route window → Destination on another plan, then 🌀 Next portal at the portal.

Deleting a point deletes its links. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🌀 Inter-plan links.
aide.sec.carnet.titre: 📔 My logbook — the history of your outings
aide.sec.carnet.html:
Each visit to a map becomes an outing: date, duration, distance, additions, route, photos, note.

Where: 📔 My logbook in 🧰 Tools on the home screen; on a map, 📊 Session details → 📔 Trip in progress (🏁 Close my trip, Refine track).

  • Filing: archived automatically after your visit; 🏁 files it right away.
  • 🚶 Field trip or 🖥️ desk work: sorted on its own, fixable from its sheet.
  • 📖 Stories: Story mode notes and PDFs of all your maps.

📔 Start an outing by hand: the 📔 Start an outing button in 📊 Session details. Details: 📖 Documentation › 📔 My logbook — the history of your outings.

aide.sec.heatmap.html:
🧩 Optional feature, off by default: turn it on in ⚙️ Configuration › 🧩 Optional features.

The 🔥 Heatmap tile of the 🧭 Tracker menu colours the map by how often places are visited: red = heavily used, blue = little explored.

🗂️Sources, combinable — the tracker path, your points, paths, zones and structures, and the map's data.🎚️Radius and Intensity, live — if everything is pale, raise the intensity; if everything is red, lower it.🏗️🏗️ Levels to include — on a multi-level map, to keep only some floors and compare them.

Useful to spot the routes really taken, or the sectors to check again in the field. Purely visual: it changes neither the map, nor your annotations, nor the exports. Rescue mode keeps its own activity heatmap. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 🔥 Heatmap.
aide.sec.vibration.html:
🧩 Optional feature, off by default: turn it on in ⚙️ Configuration › 🧩 Optional features.

A short vibration confirms actions: itinerary step reached, recalibration, step validated, Rescue mode alerts (team running late, missing members).

🚨 Survival alerts always vibrate, even with the option off: emergency exit found or not found, critical alert broadcast. On iPhone, the option is greyed out and nothing vibrates: iOS does not give vibration to web pages. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🔭 Going further › 📳 Haptic vibration.
aide.sec.je-suis-perdu.html:
You no longer know where you are. 🧭 Tracker › ⛑️ I'm lost — Emergency mode estimates the area where you may be. It is a geometric aid: it does not replace good reflexes, listed under 📚 Best practices at the top of the window.

  1. Last known position: a point searched by name, 📍 Click map or 🧭 Tracker position.
  2. ⏱️ Elapsed time (1 to 90 min) and 🏃 walking speed: the area's radius is speed × time.
  3. 🔮 Visual clues (optional): what you see, separated by commas. The app looks for them in the name, note and tags of the points.
  4. 🎯 Compute the zone: orange circle = the area, purple 🔮 = a clue inside the area, purple circle = your most likely position.

Then: 📋 Copy report (a message ready for a text or the radio), ✅ Delete the zone and save my presumed position (places a ⚠️ point), 🗑️ Clear the zone and close, or 👁️ Close to keep the area on the map. Details: 📖 Documentation › ⛑️ I'm lost.
aide.sec.urgence-xl.html:
You know where you are but need the essentials in very large print. 🧭 Tracker › 🔆 XL display (position + heading) opens a full screen that fits without scrolling:

  • 🗺️ A mini-map centred on you, with a giant compass and the map's points. Drag or pinch it to look further; 🎯 Recenter brings it back to you.
  • 📍 Recognise a point? Tap it, then 📍 I am here: tracking is realigned on it.
  • 📋 Georeferenced map: the 📋 icon at the top right shows your GPS coordinates in large print, to read out to rescuers, and copies them for a text message. It also says if your position has never been confirmed.
  • 🪧 The next guidance instruction, if a route is drawn.

The screen does not go to sleep. To leave: ↩️ EXIT XL DISPLAY, at the bottom, or Esc. To find a way out, use 🚨 Emergency exit; if you no longer know where you are, ⛑️ I'm lost.
aide.sec.itineraire.html:
🧭 Tracker › 🗺️ Compute a route finds the shortest path along the map's paths.

  1. Add your 📍 waypoints in order: map click, 🔍 search or 🧭 your position.
  2. 🎯 Compute route: the route appears in cyan, with its distance and an estimated time based on your pace.
  3. 💾 Save as route keeps it in your session.

While walking: 📍 I am here on a point of the route removes the part already done and validates the stop. Elsewhere, the app offers to recompute, keep the route or delete it.

🪧 Guidance: as soon as your position is known, a banner says “In 40 m, turn left”. Tapping it opens the roadmap. Its ✕ turns guidance off; the 🪧 tile of the Tracker menu turns it back on.

⛔ Inaccessible zones are never crossed; other points, tags or zones can be avoided under 🚫 Avoidance preferences. Distances are approximate: the position drifts. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🗺️ Computing a route.
aide.sec.corriger.html:
🧹 Erase, in the 🛣️ Paths, ⬛ Zones and 🏛️ Structures groups: ↩️ Last point (a missed tap), ✂️ Last object, 🎯 Select the object to delete on the map, or 🗑️ All.

One specific object: tap it; its bubble has 🗑️ Delete and 🔄 Convert. Converting changes its type, or its family for the same shape: a line stays a line (a working face can become a gallery and enter route computing), a surface stays a surface.

Several objects at once: in the conversion window, 🎯 Select several objects to convert, tap them, then ✅ Convert.

No confirmation: everything is undone with ⏪ (Ctrl+Z), a batch in one go. Only your objects can be changed; those of the map or of a data layer are read-only. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🧹 Erase and correct.
aide.sec.multi-niveau.html:
On a multi-storey map, every object belongs to a level (0 = reference, 1, 2… above, −1, −2… below). The yellow pill under the zoom buttons shows the active level; a tap opens 🏗️ Levels:

  • 🎯 Active level: everything you draw takes this level. [ − ] and [ + ] add one.
  • 👁️ Visible levels: the storeys to display. Unticking 0 also hides the map image: the 🖼️ Show the base plan box (≡ Filters) follows 0 until you touch it, then your choice wins; Show all sets it back to automatic.
  • Change an object's level: Level list in its sheet (path, zone, structure) or its form (POI). ⏪ undoes it. A junction: tap it, its sheet changes its two levels (Start / End) and its note.

🪜 Inter-level junction (🛣️ Paths): a gentle slope between two levels. Choose both levels, tap the points, press 🪜 again.

↕️ Stairs or shaft between levels (point): place a point of type Stairs, Rung shaft or Shaft without rungs between levels, tick the levels it serves, then confirm the gallery offered on each level (within 5 m). A shaft without rungs is only used with 🧗 Team equipped (rope) (route › Avoidances). These passages are never offered as an exit.

Without a junction, no route changes level, even if two galleries cross on screen. Multi-level mode is enabled by the map's creator: on a map without it, none of this appears. Details: 📖 Documentation › 🏗️ Multi-level mode.

bienvenue.accroche: Offline and without GPS, on phone or computer. Free and with no account: your maps and annotations stay on your device.
bienvenue.plans.intro: A map is a high-resolution image, on one or more levels, prepared in the Generator and loaded from a .zip file. You add your points, paths, zones and structures on it.
bienvenue.plans.l1: Photos attached to points, customisable legend.
bienvenue.plans.l2: Distance and area measurement, undo and redo.
bienvenue.plans.l3: Search across all your maps, links from one map to another.

bienvenue.reperer.iti.texte: The shortest way through the galleries, from one level to another; a banner tells you “In 40 m, turn left”.
bienvenue.reperer.urgence.texte: One tap: the nearest open exit, along the real path, computed on the device, with no network.
bienvenue.reperer.secours.texte: Coordination between an operator and teams, scenarios, reports.
bienvenue.reperer.legende: Tracking moves by step and compass, optionally snapped to the paths; the route follows the network.
bienvenue.prive.intro: Once opened with a connection, the app works entirely offline. Your annotations, sessions and maps stay on your device: nothing is sent to a server or to a third-party service.
bienvenue.prive.l1: Free, no account, no ads, no audience tracking.
bienvenue.prive.l2: Only outside site contacted: OpenStreetMap, for the OSM View background, can be turned off.
